text: I'll start by looking at the workspace structure and the pagination code.
The bug is visible: `end = start + page_size - 1` makes the slice exclude one item per page. Let me confirm with the tests.

The failing test confirms it. With 11 items and page size 5, page 1 returns `[1,2,3,4]`, page 2 returns `[6,7,8,9]`, and page 3 returns `[11]`. Items 5, 10 are dropped, which matches the "regular interval" in the report (every `page_size`-th item, i.e. every 5th position).

args.root_cause: In `paginate()`, the slice end index is computed as `end = start + page_size - 1` and then used as an exclusive bound in `items[start:end]`. This makes every page one item short: the last item of each full page (positions 5, 10, ... for page_size=5) is silently dropped. Those items never appear on any page, and the gap repeats at every page boundary, matching the report. The correct exclusive end is `start + page_size` (or slice `items[start:start + page_size]`). The off-by-one is only visible on full pages; the final partial page still returns the remaining items because the slice clamps at the list length.  With 11 items and page size 5, pages yield [1,2,3,4], [6,7,8,9], [11], so items 5 and 10 are lost (2 of 11 missing).

evidence.quote:
start = (page_number - 1) * page_size
    end = start + page_size - 1
    return Page(
        items=items[start:end],

assert [1, 2, 3, 4] == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
E     
E     Right contains one more item: 5
